name: Certificate Authority Security Assessment
description: Assessment of certificate authority (CA) infrastructure including root and intermediate CA security, certificate issuance policies, CA key protection, registration authority controls, and PKI architecture review. Covers both public and private/enterprise CA deployments.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to CA security assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands CA architecture and the role of root and intermediate CAs
evidence: Can explain the CA hierarchy (root, intermediate, issuing) and trust model
Understands the difference between public and private CA deployments
Can describe why root CA key protection is critical

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Reviews basic CA configurations and policies under supervision
evidence: Inspects CA certificate extensions (basic constraints, key usage, name constraints) under guidance
Reviews certificate policy (CP) and certification practice statement (CPS) documents
Identifies overly permissive issuing CA configurations
Documents CA assessment findings following lab templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses enterprise CA infrastructure for security weaknesses
evidence: Evaluates CA key protection mechanisms (HSM usage, key ceremony procedures)
Assesses certificate issuance controls and template security (AD CS, EJBCA)
Identifies misconfigured certificate templates enabling privilege escalation (ESC1-ESC8+ patterns)
Produces findings referencing CA/Browser Forum requirements or NIST SP 800-57

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex CA assessment scenarios; evaluates PKI architecture design
evidence: Assesses multi-tier PKI architectures for design weaknesses
Evaluates cross-certification and bridge CA trust models
Identifies AD CS attack paths (CVE-2022-26923 / Certifried, ESC variants) and validates exploitability
Reviews and mentors junior staff on CA security assessment methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines CA assessment methodology; recognised authority on PKI architecture security
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's CA security assessment methodology
Published research on CA compromise, misissuance, or PKI architecture flaws
Provides expert guidance on PKI architecture design and CA hardening
Trains teams on CA internals, trust models, and assessment approaches

assessment_methods.description: Assess an enterprise AD CS deployment: review certificate templates, CA permissions, and issuance controls; identify privilege escalation paths
Review CA security assessment findings from a recent engagement for completeness and risk accuracy
